senses.def: to spend time outdoors, with the possible implication of living outdoors

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to an unlimited duration of time
pertaining to being pure in the sense of not being diluted and hence at full strength
a surface of hard ground or stone where grain was threshed out, either by beating or having animals trample upon it
senses.comment: The meaning of ἅλων as ‘threshing floor’ forms the basis for the figurative extension of meaning (a metonymy) referring to the threshed grain still lying on the threshing floor (see 3.43). The meaning may be made clear by rendering ‘to thresh out completely all of the grain.’ On the other hand, it is possible to interpret ἅλων in Matthew 3:12 in a literal sense and translate ‘he will clean up his threshing floor,’ that is, by gathering up the grain and getting rid of the straw and chaff.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἅλων[a] ‘threshing floor,’ 7.65) grain in the process of being threshed
senses.comment: ἅλων in Matthew 3:12 may also be interpreted as a threshing floor (see 7.65).

senses.def: (derivative of ἀνάγκη[b] ‘complete obligation,’ 71.30) pertaining to being obligatory on the basis of being imposed
to cause the process of burning to begin
senses.comment: As already noted in the series of terms listed in 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.|It is possible that ἀνάπτω differs from ἅπτω either in the intensity of the activity or with special emphasis upon the initial phase of setting something on fire.

senses.def: a human being (normally an adult)
glosses: (in the singular) person, human being, individual
senses.comment: In Matthew 14:35 (ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ‘when the people of that place recognized him’) one may argue that οἱ ἄνδρες refers specifically to males, but the context would seem to indicate that the reference is to people in general. In translation a pronominal expression may frequently be employed when ἀνήρ[b] occurs in the text, for example, ‘when those who lived in that place recognized him’.|It is not uncommon in languages for a term which is often used to refer to an adult male to be employed also in a generic sense of ‘person.’ This is especially true when such terms are used in the plural form.|In a number of instances, generic meanings of receptor languages have not been recognized as such, since translators have assumed that such receptor-language terms refer only to members of a particular tribe or group (because they have been found only in specific contexts), while in reality such terms often designate people in general. One must, however, be on the alert for seemingly generic terms which refer only to the so-called ‘in-group,’ that is to say, members of a particular tribe, society, or community.

senses.def: an adult male person of marriageable age
a man who is married to a woman
senses.comment: ἀνήρ in the meaning of ‘husband’ is normally clearly marked by context, usually involving a so- called ‘possessive marker,’ though in some contexts such as John 4:17 and Matthew 19:10, the distinctions in meaning are quite clear, but it is only from each individual context that one can determine whether ἀνήρ means simply ‘man’ (see 9.24) or ‘husband.’ See also discussion at 10.54.

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: the outside person) the physical nature or aspect of a person
senses.comment: The phrase ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος is to be understood in direct contrast with ὁ ἔσω (ἄνθρωπος) in the same verse, which refers to the psychological or spiritual nature of human personality (see 26.1).

senses.def: (idioms, literally: the inner (person), and: the hidden (person)) the psychological faculty, including intellectual, emotional, and spiritual aspects, in contrast with the purely physical aspects of human existence
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is quite impossible to speak of the psychological faculty of a person as being merely ‘that which is within.’ It is frequently necessary to refer to a particular organ of the body, for example, ‘the heart’ or ‘the liver’ or ‘the spleen.’ In some languages, however, one may refer to this faculty as being ‘the person who stands inside’ or ‘the real person’ or even ‘the other person.’|In Luke 17:21 the phrase ἐντὸς ὑμῶν in the statement ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν look, God’s reign is within you may constitute a reference to the same inner being designated by the phrases ὁ ἔσω and ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ. On this basis some scholars have suggested that the phrase ἐντὸς ὑμῶν can be interpreted as a potentiality for participation and hence be translated within your grasp, but it is more likely that one should understand the phrase ἐντὸς ὑμῶν in Luke 17:21 as a spacial relationship, for example, ‘in your midst’ or ‘among you’ (see 83.9).

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: old person, or: former person) the old or former pattern of behavior, in contrast with a new pattern of behavior which people should conform to
senses.comment: In a number of languages one can best render this expression in Ephesians 4:22 as ‘don’t live the way you used to.’

senses.def: (a Semitic idiom, literally: sons of men) human beings (equivalent in denotative meaning to ἄνθρωπος[a], 9.1)
senses.comment: It is rare indeed that one can reproduce literally the Semitic phrase ‘sons of men,’ since the expression is likely to be interpreted as relating only to the male offspring of fathers.

senses.def: a title with Messianic implications used by Jesus concerning himself
senses.comment: This title ‘Son of Man’ served not only to affirm but also to hide Christ’s Messianic role.|In a number of languages there are serious complications involved in a literal translation of υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ‘Son of Man.’ In the first place, this is likely to be understood in a more or less literal sense of ‘son of a man’ and thus a denial of the virgin birth. Such is particularly true in languages which have two words for ‘son,’ one meaning ‘son of a man’ and the other, ‘son of a woman.’ Under such circumstances, a literal translation would be a clear denial of the virgin birth.

senses.def: pertaining to not offering any special benefit
(derivative of ἀποβάλλω ‘to reject,’ not occurring in the NT) that which is to be rejected
senses.comment: The closest equivalent of ἀπόβλητος in a number of languages is ‘something to be thrown away’ or ‘something to refuse.’

senses.def: to pull or draw away from or out of
(figurative extension of meaning of ἀποσπάω[a] ‘to pull out, to drag,’ 15.214) to cause a change of belief so as to correspond more with the beliefs of the person or factor causing the change
to draw oneself away from, suggesting that the movement was not sudden
a companion of Paul
(derivative of ἀσθενέω[a] ‘to be weak,’ 74.26) an instance of weakness or limited capacity
senses.comment: In some languages it may be appropriate to translate τὰ ἀσθενήματα as ‘times when they are weak.’

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: to lodge in a place during the night
a Semitic deity
(derivative of Βέροια ‘Beroea,’ 93.422) a person who lives in or is a native of Beroea
general word for individual cattle; may be male (bull or ox) or female (cow); plural: cattle
senses.comment: In most contexts βοῦς (masc. gender) would seem to refer to an ox (in contrast with ταῦρος ‘bull,’ 4.16). In the plural form βοῦς may be translated simply as a collective ‘cattle.’|Though in a number of languages a very special distinction is made between ‘bulls’ and ‘oxen’ (or ‘steers’), no such marked difference occurs in NT usage, and there appears to be no need of introducing any artificial distinction in particular passages.

senses.def: (derivative of γενεαλογέομαι ‘to be descended from,’ 10.25) a list of direct descendants or ascendants
the corner of an area or construction, either an inside corner or an outside corner
a person in charge of guarding a jail or prison
to fight or contend with, involving severity and thoroughness
possibly a street crossing, but more probably the place where a principal thoroughfare crosses a city boundary and extends into the open country
glosses: where a main street leaves the city (possibly at the city wall)

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to deceive by using trickery and falsehood
to move nearer to a reference point
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is not possible to merely say ‘to come near,’ for it is necessary to specify the reference point, in other words, ‘near to what?’ One may accordingly translate this expression in Luke 18:40 as ‘when he came near to Jesus, Jesus asked him.’

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: the occurrence of a point of time close to a subsequent point of time
senses.comment: Though in many languages time may be expressed in terms of space, as in speaking of ‘time coming near,’ in other languages this may not be at all possible. Accordingly, this clause in Matthew 21:34 may need to be translated as ‘it was about time to harvest’ or ‘when it was about time to gather the grapes.’

senses.def: to bring or lead into
to carry or bring something into an area or structure
to change to a state in which something is lacking or insufficient
senses.comment: ‘To give out’ may be expressed as ‘to no longer exist’ or ‘no longer to have any.’

senses.def: to depart out of a place
senses.comment: This meaning is only found as a variant reading: κἀκείνους κατέ λειπεν ἐκεῖ καὶ ἔκλειπεν ‘he left them behind there and departed’ Acts 18:19 (apparatus).

senses.def: to cease from an activity which has gone on for some time
senses.comment: In this phrase in Luke 23:45 there is an evident ellipsis of an expression meaning ‘to shine.’

senses.def: to cease, of a state, with the implication of nothing of the state continuing to exist
to state that someone has done wrong, with the implication that there is adequate proof of such wrongdoing
(derivative of ἐμπορεύομαι[a] ‘to be in business,’ 57.196) one who is engaged in commerce and trade
to cause hardship by continual annoyance
to undergo hardship from continual annoyance
motion from or out of a region (in Hebrews 11:22, the only occurrence of ἔξοδος[a] in the NT, the reference is to Israels departure from Egypt)
to depart from life, as a euphemistic expression for death

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: any type of outer garment
senses.comment: The choice of an equivalent for these terms relating to ‘outer garments’ will depend largely upon the specific context and the usage in each receptor language. The most common equivalent is a term meaning ‘coat.’

senses.def: (derivative of ἐπιορκέω[b] ‘to swear falsely,’ 33.465) one who swears falsely
to observe something, implying both continuity and intent
senses.comment: The phrase ‘they will observe’ (1 Peter 3:2) may be expressed in some languages as ‘they will constantly see’ or ‘they will always see.’

senses.subdomain: Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
senses.def: pertaining to that which causes someone to be pleased
speaking of something in favorable terms
any living creature, whether wild or domesticated (in contrast with plants)
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘living things’ or ‘living creatures’ is simply ‘those which are alive’ or ‘those that move about.’ ζῷον[a], therefore, includes essentially quadrupeds, fish, birds, and insects, and is not used in the NT to designate human beings. In several passages in the book of Revelation, ζῷον[b] ‘a living being’ (12.32) is employed to refer to supernatural beings at God’s throne (note Revelation 4:6 which in many ways is similar to the description of ‘living creatures’ in f).

senses.def: a supernatural being surrounding the throne of God in visions of the book of Revelation
senses.comment: The OT parallel for the ζῷον in Revelation is to be found in -.

senses.def: (derivative of θαυμάζω ‘to be amazed,’ 25.213) pertaining to that which causes or is worthy of amazement and wonder

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: a small amount of blood in coagulated form
that which is being urgently requested by a suppliant
the central figure of the book of Job
to suffer physical pain, hardship and distress
senses.comment: In rendering ‘endure suffering’ (2 Timothy 4:5), one must often expand somewhat the number of lexical items in order to convey the correct meaning, for example, ‘continue doing what you should even though you are suffering’ or ‘remain firm even though people cause you suffering.’

senses.def: to try to learn the location of an object by diligently following after or tracking down
to communicate by means of a sign or signal
senses.comment: The rendering of this statement in Acts 12:17 must often be modified depending upon the particular nature of the signal in the receptor language, for example, ‘by holding up his hand, he told them to be quiet’ or ‘he motioned with his hand and they understood they should be quiet.’

senses.def: the process of burning
senses.comment: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in the use of terms for burning. For example, the burning of a substance for light, as in the case of a lamp or candle, may be indicated by a term quite different from an expression indicating the destruction or burning up of something. Similarly, the burning of wood for cooking may require still another term. The extent or size of the fire involved may also require some distinctions in terms for burning.

senses.def: (derivative of κλάω ‘to break,’ 19.34) a fragment or piece resulting from the action of breaking
to carry or bring something to someone, usually implying a transfer
to cause someone to experience something on the basis of what that person has already done
glosses: to cause to experience in return
to cause to experience in proportion to

senses.def: to receive as a type of compensation
to receive back something which one has previously possessed or its equivalent
to cause to be safe or protected by hiding, in some contexts with the intent of not being found
senses.comment: Since κρύπτω also means ‘to make invisible,’ some scholars believe that this statement in Colossians 3:3 means that ‘your life is concealed in Christ’ or ‘… hidden from view …’ (see 24.30). For another interpretation of κρύπτω in Matthew 13:44, see 24.29.

senses.def: to cause something to be invisible, with the intent of its being not found
senses.comment: For another interpretation of κρύπτω in Matthew 13:44, see 21.12.

senses.def: to cause something to be invisible (in the sense of being hidden), but for the purpose of safekeeping and protection
senses.comment: The evident implication of this statement in Colossians 3:3 is to emphasize the fact that the true life of the believer is not some material, visible object or happening, but something spiritual and thus only visible to those spiritually enlightened or concerned. For another interpretation of κρύπτω in Colossians 3:3, see 21.12.

senses.subdomain: Not Able To Be Known, Secret
senses.def: to cause something not to be known
senses.comment: In a number of languages, the causative relationships involved in Matthew 11:25 must be made somewhat more explicit, for example, ‘because you have kept the wise and learned people from knowing and have caused the unlearned to know.’ In Matthew 11:25 νήπιος is used figuratively in reference to unlearned people.

senses.def: to shine or to produce light, as in the case of heavenly bodies, lightning, candles, torches, etc.
senses.comment: Terms for ‘shining, giving light’ often differ depending upon the type of source. There may be, for example, a contrast between the shining of a heavenly body in contrast with some source on earth. There may also be a difference between a continuous shining such as of the sun and the moon and a brief flash, as in the case of lightning or sparks from a fire.

senses.def: the content of various utterances
(derivative of Μακεδονία ‘Macedonia,’ 93.527) a person who is a native of Macedonia

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: crafty scheming with the intent to deceive
to cause a change of state, with emphasis upon the difference in the resulting state
glosses: to cause to be different from

senses.def: to recall information from memory, but without necessarily the implication that persons have actually forgotten
senses.comment: In some languages the process of remembering is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to find one’s thoughts again’ or ‘to see again in one’s heart’ or ‘to have one’s liver repeat the words.’

senses.def: (compare μνημονεύω[a] ‘to remember, to recall,’ 29.7) to keep on recalling and thinking about again and again
glosses: to think about again and again

senses.subdomain: Recalling and Responding with Appropriate Action
senses.def: to recall or be aware of information, and as a result to respond in an appropriate manner (for example, punishing, helping, honoring, etc., depending upon the context)
senses.comment: μνημονεύω in Revelation 18:5 implies much more than God’s mental state in remembering the crimes of Babylon. The reference is clearly to God’s both remembering and punishing. Similarly, in Galatians 2:10 μνημονεύω refers to more than mere mental awareness of those in need, for the process of recall involves doing something about the needy (compare 29.7). In a number of languages it may be necessary to make this implication quite specific, for example, ‘all they asked was that we should be concerned for the needy of their group.’

senses.subdomain: Recalling and Responding with Appropriate Action
senses.def: to recall and to respond by making mention of
to have an unhealthy or morbid desire for something
glosses: to desire in an unhealthy manner
senses.comment: In some languages the closest equivalent of ‘an unhealthy desire’ would be ‘to desire something that one should not desire.’

senses.subdomain: Groups and Members of Groups of Persons Regarded as Related by Blood but without Special Reference to Successive Generations
senses.def: (derivative of οἶκος[b] ‘family,’ 10.8) one who belongs to a particular household or extended family
a marker of concession, with the possible implication of an added aspect of similarity
senses.comment: The interpretation of ὅμως in Galatians 3:15 and 1 Corinthians 14:7 as indicating concession is doubtful, and it may be preferable to understand ὅμως in these contexts as meaning ‘likewise’ or ‘similarly,’ for example, ‘similarly, in the case of a human will, no one annuls it’ and ‘similarly, in the case of a flute or harp, lifeless instruments which produce a sound’ (see 64.11).

senses.def: pertaining to being, at least in some respects, similar
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ὅμως in Galatians 3:15, see 89.74.

senses.def: a marker of an implied clause of concession

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: indefinite and multiple points of time, simultaneous with other corresponding points of time
a person who guides, directs, and shows concern for
senses.comment: It may be difficult to render appropriately ἐπίτροπος[b] and παιδαγωγός with a combined meaning of guiding and caring for. It may, in fact, be necessary in some instances to use two verbal expressions, for example, ‘to guide and to help’ or ‘to help by leading’ or ‘to care for by leading.’|In classical times, a παιδαγωγός was a man, usually a slave, whose task it was to conduct a boy to and from school and to supervise and direct his general conduct. He was not a teacher.

senses.def: (a title for the Holy Spirit) one who helps, by consoling, encouraging, or mediating on behalf of
senses.comment: The principal difficulty encountered in rendering παράκλητος is the fact that this term covers potentially such a wide area of meaning. The traditional rendering of ‘Comforter’ is especially misleading because it suggests only one very limited aspect of what the Holy Spirit does. A term such as ‘Helper’ is highly generic and can be particularly useful in some languages. In certain instances, for example, the concept of ‘Helper’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘the one who mothers us’ or, as in one language in Central Africa, ‘the one who falls down beside us,’ that is to say, an individual who upon finding a person collapsed along the road, kneels down beside the victim, cares for his needs, and carries him to safety.|A rendering based upon the concept of legal advocate seems in most instances to be too restrictive. Furthermore, there may be quite unsatisfactory connotations associated with any word which suggests a lawyer, especially since in so many societies, a lawyer is thought of primarily as one who ‘bribes the judges’ or ‘can speak two truths’ or, as in one language, is ‘a professional liar.’ See also παράκλητος 35.16 and especially its footnote.

senses.def: (derivative of παρακαλέω ‘to call upon to provide help,’ not occurring in this specific sense in the NT) one who may be called upon to provide help or assistance
one of the seven helpers in the church in Jerusalem
cardinal number, where there are five thousand instances of a countable entity
to run or go hurriedly about
to strike or hit an object, one or more times
senses.comment: One may also render this expression in Luke 12:48 as ‘does something for which he should be beaten.’

senses.def: the condition resulting from being severely hurt or wounded
a widespread contagious disease, often associated with divine retribution
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret πληγή in Revelation 11:6 as being somewhat more generic in meaning, that is to say, trouble or distress causing widespread suffering (see 22.13).

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of πληγή[c] ‘plague,’ 23.158) a type of trouble or distress causing widespread and/or intense suffering
senses.comment: One may also render Revelation 18:4 as ‘so that you will not suffer as she is going to suffer.’

senses.def: (derivative of Πόντος ‘Pontus,’ 93.555) pertaining to Pontus
the area in front of an entrance to a building
senses.comment: προαύλιον may be rendered as ‘in front of the building.’

senses.def: to provide sufficiently in addition (a more emphatic expression than πληρόω[d], 35.33)

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to make unjust distinctions between people by treating one person better than another
senses.comment: ‘To show favoritism’ or ‘to be partial’ is expressed in an idiomatic manner in some languages, for example, ‘to look only upon a person’s face,’ ‘to call a sparrow a chicken,’ or ‘to give one’s clansman the best piece of meat.’

senses.def: to cause to be hot, as of fire
the process of burning
senses.comment: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in the use of terms for burning. For example, the burning of a substance for light, as in the case of a lamp or candle, may be indicated by a term quite different from an expression indicating the destruction or burning up of something. Similarly, the burning of wood for cooking may require still another term. The extent or size of the fire involved may also require some distinctions in terms for burning.|In a number of languages it is extremely difficult to indicate burning as means simply by a phrase such as ‘by burning.’ Normally, burning can only be referred to by means of an expression referring to fire. Accordingly, 2 Peter 3:12 may be rendered as ‘a great fire will destroy the sky and will cause the elements to melt’; likewise, in Acts 28:2 one may translate ‘in the end a great fire will destroy the earth.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of πυρόω[b] ‘to burn,’ 14.63) to be upset, with great concern and anxiety
to experience intense sexual desire
to cause something to move back and forth rapidly, often violently
senses.comment: In some languages there are quite distinct terms for shaking, depending upon the vigor of the motion and/or the objects which are shaken. Accordingly, one must exercise care in selecting terms which will accurately and adequately represent the nature of the shaking in the various contexts. For example, in Hebrews 12:26 the shaking would presumably involve some kind of reverberation, but in Revelation 6:13 the action of the wind suggests whipping something back and forth.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of σείω[a] ‘to shake,’ 16.7) to cause extreme anxiety and apprehension, implying accompanying movement
to shake or tremble, often with the implication of fear and/or consternation
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are two distinct terms for trembling, one relating to illness (as in the case of epileptic seizures or the chills and fever associated with malaria) and the other associated with fear.

senses.def: shade, as a shelter from light and the heat associated with light
senses.comment: A term for ‘shade’ as an area sheltered from the direct rays of the sun usually differs from a term for ‘shadow,’ which is cast by a particular object blocking rays of light (see 14.61).

senses.def: the shape or shade cast by an object which blocks rays of light
senses.comment: In Luke 1:79 (τοῖς ἐν σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις ‘those living in the darkness and shadow of death’), σκιά may be interpreted as being used figuratively of a shadow cast by impending death, that is to say, death is personified in such a way as to suggest that it casts a shadow because of its nearness. One may, therefore, translate τοῖς ἐν σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις as ‘those who live in the darkness of impending death,’ in which case σκιά becomes essentially equivalent to an expression of time.|In a number of languages a term for ‘shadow’ has a number of very important meanings. In some instances it is regarded as a part of personality which goes on to the next world, since a dead person no longer ‘casts a shadow.’ The shadow may also be regarded as a kind of counterpart of the personality, a type of alter ego. In cases of severe illness one may say ‘his shadow has walked away,’ and in many parts of the world the shadow of a person is an important element in the practice of black magic, for to damage a shadow may be regarded as a means of causing harm to a person.

senses.def: a faint archetype which foreshadows a later reality

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: pertaining to being earnest and diligent in undertaking an activity
senses.comment: In a number of languages eagerness can only be expressed in terms of desire. Hence, for Philippians 2:28 one must sometimes translate ‘I am all the more desirous of sending him to you.”

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being hated or regarded as worthy of being hated
one who joins others as an imitator
glosses: to be an imitator together with others

senses.def: the movement of two or more objects to the same location
senses.comment: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

senses.def: to be together with someone
to groan or to sigh together with someone else
senses.comment: In Romans 8:22 συστενάζω is used figuratively. It may be difficult to speak of ‘all of creation groans together,’ since the phrase ‘all of creation’ would seem to be a total unit. It may therefore be necessary to translate ‘all of creation groans together’ as ‘all parts of the creation groan together’ or ‘everything that has been created is groaning at the same time.’

senses.subdomain: Assign to a Role or Function
senses.def: to assign someone to a particular task, function, or role
senses.comment: Though τάσσω in Acts 13:48 has sometimes been interpreted as meaning ‘to choose,’ there seems to be far more involved than merely a matter of selection, since a relationship is specifically assigned.

senses.def: to cause someone to be in a state involving an order or arrangement
to give detailed instructions as to what must be done
to propose something to someone
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand τάσσω in Acts 28:23 as meaning ‘to arrange,’ but in Acts 28:23 it would seem that τάσσω implies not only proposing a date but obtaining an agreement.

senses.def: to do something with devotion, with the possible implication of systematic, regular activity

senses.subdomain: Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
senses.def: honor as an element in the assignment of status to a person
the worth or merit of some object, event, or state
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘value’ is almost always in terms of ‘importance.’ This is particularly true if one is speaking of objects which are normally not bought and sold. Accordingly, one may render this particular expression in 1 Corinthians 12:23 as ‘those parts of the body which we think of as not being so important, to these we grant particular importance’ or ‘… we consider as being very important.’|It is also possible to interpret τιμή in 1 Corinthians 12:23 as a degree of honor or appreciation (see τιμή[a], 87.4).

senses.def: the amount of money or property regarded as representing the value or price of something
senses.comment: It would be wrong to assume that τιμή in 1 Corinthians 7:23 necessarily means ‘a high price.’ The notion ‘high’ comes from the contextual reference to the death of Christ. In 1 Corinthians 7:23, however, the implication is that a price was set and that the payment has been made. If the passive expression in 1 Corinthians 7:23 must be made active, one may translate as ‘Christ bought you with a price’ or ‘Christ paid for you.’

senses.def: compensation given for special service, with the implication that this is a way by which honor or respect may be shown
senses.comment: τιμή[d] in the sense of compensation is related in meaning to τιμάω[c] to support, to provide for (57.117) and τιμή[c] cost (57.161), but in 1 Timothy 5:17 it is also possible to understand τιμή in the sense of τιμή[a] honor, respect (87.4), and therefore one may speak of the elders as receiving double honor.

senses.def: a relatively deep concave dish used for holding or cooking food or liquids; usually made of clay, but also metals
senses.comment: In the two NT occurrences (Matthew 26:23; Mark 14:20) τρύβλιον can be understood as a part of an idiom (literally ‘to dip one’s hands into the bowl with someone’) meaning ‘to share a meal with someone.’ If, however, the idiom is to be translated literally (and this is normally the case), there are certain difficulties involved, since a literal rendering of ‘to dip one’s hand into a bowl’ might mean literally putting one’s fingers or hand into a bowl rather than dipping in food which one holds in the hand. An idiomatic interpretation of ‘sharing a meal with someone’ or ‘eating together with’ may be preferable. But if one does translate the idiom somewhat literally, it is important in some languages to render this phrase as ‘to dip food into a bowl together with someone’ or ‘to jointly dip food into sauce.’

senses.def: to increase exceedingly in the degree of a state
to bring something under the firm control of someone
to submit to the orders or directives of someone
a broad, shallow bowl, normally used for cooking or for serving liquids
the psychological faculty of thoughtful planning, often with the implication of being wise and provident
